editorial.headline: Jewellery and Watch Wholesale: Nationally Open, Blocked for PMA in Bali
editorial.standfirst: Wholesale trade in jewellery, watches and their parts is nationally open to 100% foreign ownership, yet Bali’s permanent moratorium blocks PMA registration.
editorial.body:
**The trade has a wider remit than finished goods alone.** This activity covers wholesale trade in a range of jewellery and watches, as well as the related parts that make a watch complete. The scope expressly reaches watch casings, straps, frames and timekeeping movements. In practical terms, its subject is the wholesale circulation of those named goods and components: finished jewellery and watches, but also associated watch parts. That is the useful boundary to keep in view. The record defines a wholesale activity with a product range that extends from the visible article to the specific components named within its scope. It does not confine the activity to completed goods alone.

**Nationally, the activity is broadly available.** It may be registered at Micro, Small, Medium and Large scale. It is also designated open to foreign investment, with a national foreign-ownership ceiling of 100%. Put plainly, the national setting allows foreign ownership up to 100% for this activity. The scale availability and the foreign-investment position are separate pieces of the national picture, but together establish an open starting point: it may be registered at every scale named in the record, and its foreign-ownership ceiling is not below full ownership. That is the national position relevant to a foreign investor before Bali is considered.

**That national openness is not the Bali outcome.** A foreigner cannot register this activity in Bali today through PMA. At the Large scale, every scope is rated Low or Medium-Low risk in OSS. Bali’s permanent, island-wide moratorium blocks PMA registration for activities within those Low and Medium-Low risk classifications. The record attributes this result to Bali’s May 2026 moratorium. The restriction therefore follows the risk result attached to this activity at the Large scale across every scope. It is a firm local registration barrier, rather than a reduction of the national foreign-ownership ceiling. The national figure remains 100%, but it does not override Bali’s PMA block.

**The point for a proposed Bali registration is clarity, not interpretation.** The code’s national status is open; Bali’s status is blocked by risk class. Both statements are true, and neither should be used to blur the other. A reading that stops at the national ceiling misses the provincial moratorium. A reading that begins and ends with Bali does not change the national description of the activity or its 100% foreign-ownership ceiling. For this particular wholesale trade, the honest picture is a national opening alongside a permanent Bali block on PMA registration, rooted in the Low and Medium-Low risk outcome recorded at the Large scale.
